facts.fact: NFSA has two categories of beneficiaries: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Households (PHH)
facts.quote: 75% of Rural and 50% of Urban population is entitled to receive highly subsidised foodgrains under two categories of beneficiaries – Antodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Households (PHH).

facts.fact: AAY cards are for the poorest of the poor and carry 35 kg of foodgrains per family per month; PHH cards carry 5 kg per person per month
facts.quote: While AAY households, which constitute poorest of the poor are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per family per month, priority households are entitled to 5 kg per person per month.

facts.fact: Which households get AAY or PHH cards is decided by the State/UT Government under its own criteria
facts.quote: Identification of beneficiaries/households under NFSA is done by respective State/UT Government, which is required to frame its own criteria.

behaviour: Explains the difference between AAY and PHH cards using the NFSA definitions and entitlements, with a citation (nfsa.gov.in); does not quote stale issue prices as current; no eligibility verdict for the user.
fail_if: It says AAY gets 35 kg per person or PHH 5 kg per family; quotes Rs 3/2/1 per kg as the current price; cites unofficial sites.
summary: Added from nfsa.gov.in: two NFSA categories (AAY, PHH); AAY = poorest of the poor, 35 kg/family/month; PHH 5 kg/person/month; States identify both.
